test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If the difference between the mean and the mode of certain observations is 69, then the difference between the mean and the median is ________.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **empirical relationship** between central tendencies is: (Mean − Mode) = 3 × (Mean − Median).

Given: Mean − Mode = 69

69 = 3 × (Mean − Median)

⇒ Mean − Median = 69 ÷ 3 = 23

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Difference between **Mean** and **Mode** (Mean − Mode) = 69.

**Formula Used:** Empirical relation: **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd9b9742537e2d323b385c828b4c3affb390a33b3af7694d9e09f5853b724f2c.png] 

From the given condition: Mean − Mode = 69

⇒ Mode = Mean − 69

Substitute the value of **Mode** in the empirical formula:

⇒ Mean − 69 = 3 Median − 2 Mean

⇒ Mean + 2 Mean − 69 = 3 Median

⇒ 3 Mean − 3 Median = 69

⇒ 3(Mean − Median) = 69

⇒ Mean − Median = 69 ÷ 3

⇒ Mean − Median = 23

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

In a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean** or (Mean − Mode) = 3 (Mean − Median).

Symmetric Distribution

For a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the values of Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Karl Pearson Coefficient of Skewness

It is calculated as Sₖ = (Mean − Mode) ÷ Standard Deviation, or 3(Mean − Median) ÷ Standard Deviation.</p
